evidence.description: The month is assigned before the throwing serialization and report decoding operation completes.

candidates.explanation: If serialization or decoding throws, latestMonth has already changed while latestReport retains its previous value. A failed update can therefore leave the publicly readable month and report describing different reporting periods.
candidates.title: Failed decoding leaves partially updated state

evidence.description: Response keys are parsed into dates and then regenerated using yyyy-M before looking up the report.

candidates.explanation: Parsing and formatting a date does not preserve the original key spelling. For example, a key such as "2023-06" can parse successfully but be formatted back as "2023-6". The subsequent lookup then misses the existing report, substitutes an empty dictionary, and fails decoding.
candidates.title: Date normalization can break response-key lookup

evidence.description: A shared instance exposes mutable month and report state without actor isolation or synchronization.
The asynchronous update suspends during the request.
Each update writes the shared properties separately.

candidates.explanation: The shared instance allows overlapping asynchronous updates and concurrent reads without synchronization. Updates can race or interleave their separate property assignments, exposing inconsistent month/report pairs; an earlier request can also overwrite the result of a later request.
candidates.title: Shared report state has no concurrency isolation

evidence.description: The parser specifies a fixed numeric date format and time zone but leaves its locale and calendar at their defaults.

candidates.explanation: A DateFormatter's default locale and calendar depend on user settings. Setting yyyy-M and UTC does not establish a Gregorian calendar, so the same response key can represent a different absolute date under a non-Gregorian calendar. That affects the selected reporting month and the date exposed to callers.
candidates.title: Machine-readable dates depend on user calendar settings
